exercise.name: Standing Leg Curl
library_steps: Stand at the machine with the roller behind one ankle, holding the handles.
Curl your heel up towards your hip, keeping your thigh still.
Lower slowly, then switch legs after your set.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing on the right leg, front of the left thigh on a pad, roller behind the left ankle, hands on the handles. Picture 1: left leg nearly straight; picture 2: left knee bent ~100 deg, heel toward the buttock, thigh still vertical. Only the working left side is lit.

setup.target: Thigh pad just above the knee, roller on the back of the lower shin; knee lined up with the machine pivot.
Standing leg straight, trunk upright, hands on the handles.

muscles.emg: Leg curls bias semitendinosus and biceps femoris short head (S1).
Gastrocnemius crosses the knee and helps flex it (S1).

muscles.role: Hold the pelvis level on the standing leg.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hip extends to lift the heel.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Keep the thigh on the pad so the knee does the work (S2).

sources.citation: Bourne MN, Williams MD, Opar DA, et al. Impact of exercise selection on hamstring muscle activation. Br J Sports Med. 2017;51(13):1021-1028.
sources.what_it_gave: Knee-flexion exercises (leg curls) bias the semitendinosus and biceps femoris short head; hip-extension exercises bias the long head.

sources.citation: Maeo S, Huang M, Wu Y, et al. Greater hamstrings muscle hypertrophy but similar damage protection after training at long versus short muscle lengths. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2021;53(4):825-837.
sources.what_it_gave: Seated vs prone leg curl: hip angle changes hamstring length; both are knee-flexion work for the hamstrings.

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
